summary:
The Airport and Airway Extension Act of 2024 extends authorizations for Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) programs and related aviation revenue provisions through May 10 or May 11, 2024, as specified. The Act operates by amending existing statutory sunset dates and authorization amounts in title 49, United States Code, the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, and other public laws.

Title I amends FAA program authorizations. Section 101(a) amends 49 U.S.C. § 48103(a) to authorize appropriations for the Airport Improvement Program (AIP) at $2,041,120,218 for October 1, 2023, through May 10, 2024. Subsection (b) provides that such sums may be obligated through September 30, 2024, and remain available until expended, subject to appropriations limitations. Subsection (c) directs the FAA Administrator to calculate AIP apportionments under 49 U.S.C. §§ 47114–47117 by first annualizing a total fiscal year 2024 amount of $3,350,000,000, then reducing all apportionments and amounts under 49 U.S.C. § 47117(b) and (f)(2) by 39 percent. Sections 101(d) and (e) extend project grant authority under 49 U.S.C. § 47104(c) and the special apportionment rule under 49 U.S.C. § 47114(c)(1)(J) by replacing “March 8, 2024” with “May 10, 2024.”

Section 102 extends 22 miscellaneous expiring authorities by striking existing March 8 or March 9, 2024, termination dates and inserting May 10 or May 11, 2024, respectively. These include: aviation insurance authority (49 U.S.C. § 44310(b)); unmanned aircraft test ranges (49 U.S.C. § 44803(h)); special authority for certain unmanned aircraft systems (49 U.S.C. § 44807(d)); airport safety and airspace hazard enforcement (49 U.S.C. § 44810(h)); competitive access reporting (49 U.S.C. § 47107(r)(3)); Marshall Islands, Micronesia, and Palau eligibility (49 U.S.C. § 47115(i)); compatible land use planning (49 U.S.C. § 47141(f)); non-movement area surveillance pilot program (49 U.S.C. § 47143(c)); the learning period for commercial space launch indemnification (51 U.S.C. § 50905(c)(9)); and several programs established in prior FAA reauthorization Acts. Subsection (g) amends 49 U.S.C. § 47115(j)(4)(A) to set supplemental discretionary funds at $340,321,762 for October 1, 2023, through May 10, 2024. Subsection (j) amends 49 U.S.C. § 48105 to authorize weather reporting programs at $23,762,295 for the same period.

Sections 103, 104, and 105 amend 49 U.S.C. §§ 106(k), 48101(a), and 48102(a) to authorize FAA Operations ($7,259,685,792), Air Navigation Facilities and Equipment ($1,794,357,923), and Research, Engineering, and Development ($155,368,852), respectively, for October 1, 2023, through May 10, 2024. Section 106 amends 49 U.S.C. §§ 41742(a)(2) and 41743(e)(2) to authorize Essential Air Service ($216,192,407) and Airports Not Receiving Sufficient Service ($6,092,896) for the same period.

Title II extends aviation revenue provisions. Section 201 amends 26 U.S.C. § 9502(d)(1) and (e)(2) to extend expenditure authority from the Airport and Airway Trust Fund through May 11, 2024, and adds a reference to this Act. Section 202 extends the taxes funding the Trust Fund through May 10 or May 11, 2024, by amending the termination dates in 26 U.S.C. §§ 4081(d)(2)(B), 4261(k)(1)(A)(ii), 4271(d)(1)(A)(ii), 4043(d), 4083(b), and 4261(j).

Title III amends 6 U.S.C. § 124n(i) to extend the Department of Homeland Security’s counter-unmanned aircraft systems authority by striking “March 9, 2024” and inserting “May 11, 2024.”
